title: Closure approve/reject endpoints are gated by generic audit.update instead of a dedicated approval permission
description: audit-closure.routes.js:20-22 registers POST /:auditId/closure/approve and /reject behind requirePermission('audit.update') — the same coarse permission that gates creating/editing CARs and findings. There is no audit.approve or audit.approve_closure permission anywhere in the module (confirmed across all route files).
preconditions: User B has audit.update (general edit rights) but is not designated an approver/lead auditor
A closure request is pending approval
steps: As User B (holds only audit.update), call POST /api/audit-assurance/:auditId/closure/approve
expectedResult: Current behavior: the call succeeds because audit.update is sufficient — there is no role distinction preventing any editor from approving audit closure. Flag for remediation: introduce a dedicated audit.approve_closure permission distinct from audit.update.

title: Audit closure approval is rejected when the approver is the same user who requested it
description: Positive control: approveClosure() (audit-closure.service.js:142-144) checks closure.approval.requestedBy.toString() === userId.toString() and throws 403 'Approver cannot be the same as the requestor (segregation of duties)'. This SoD check exists at the service layer even though the broader permission gap (H-004, AUDT-SEC-001) remains.
preconditions: UserA requested closure approval for an audit
steps: As UserA, call POST /api/audit-assurance/:auditId/closure/approve on the closure UserA just requested
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 'Approver cannot be the same as the requestor (segregation of duties)'. The closure remains in 'pending_approval' state.

title: CAR evidence confirm rejects an s3Key outside the caller's organization prefix
description: corrective-action.service.js addEvidence/uploadEvidenceFile (line 480) asserts s3Key.startsWith('evidence/${orgId}/') before accepting the file record — mirrors the same IDOR protection pattern already verified in evidence-management (EVID-SEC-003).
preconditions: Valid JWT for a user in org A
A CAR belonging to org A
steps: As an org A user, call the CAR evidence attach endpoint with a forged s3Key beginning with 'evidence/{orgB-id}/' instead of org A's prefix
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 — the s3Key does not belong to the caller's organization; no evidence subdocument referencing org B's S3 object is appended to the CAR.

title: A user can raise a finding and later close it themselves with no self-review block
description: Unlike CAR verify() (which blocks assignee===verifier), findings.controller.js updateFinding has no check comparing raisedBy to the caller closing the finding — closedBy is simply set to whoever calls the PATCH.
preconditions: UserA has audit.update permission and raised finding F (raisedBy = UserA)
steps: As UserA, call PATCH /:auditId/findings/:findingId with { status: 'closed' } on the finding UserA raised
expectedResult: Current behavior: the request succeeds and closedBy is set to UserA — the same person who raised the nonconformity closes it with no independent reviewer. Flag for remediation: add a closedBy !== raisedBy (or equivalent role-based) check analogous to the CAR verify() SoD guard.

title: CAR detail endpoint rejects requests for a carId belonging to another organization's audit
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B) each have an audit with at least one CAR
Valid JWT for a user in org A
steps: As an org A user, call GET /api/audit-assurance/:orgBAuditId/corrective-actions/:orgBCarId using org B's audit and CAR IDs
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403/404 — no CAR metadata, evidence, or verification history from org B is returned.

title: CAR evidence upload uses server-verified file metadata rather than trusting client-supplied contentType/size
description: Positive control: addEvidence/uploadEvidenceFile calls S3.getFileMetadata(s3Key) server-side to obtain real contentLength/contentType instead of trusting client-supplied values (in-code comment: 'never trust client-supplied values'), and enforces a 25MB cap plus extension/MIME allowlists (ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS, ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES).
preconditions: A presigned S3 upload URL has been generated for a CAR evidence slot
steps: Upload a file directly to the presigned URL, then call the confirm/attach endpoint declaring a mimeType/fileSize that does not match the real object
Attempt to attach a file whose extension is on the allowlist (e.g. .pdf) but whose actual content type is disallowed
expectedResult: The server's own S3.getFileMetadata lookup is used for the persisted contentType/fileSize (not the client-declared values), and the allowlist check rejects disallowed real content types even when the extension looks legitimate.
